llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a coherent static-file publish workflow, but there are packaging and install inconsistencies and a few choices (recommended curl|bash installer, metadata that omits required binaries/env) that deserve caution before installing or trusting credentials to it.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and scripts implement a static-file publishing tool that talks to https://here.now and returns a live URL — this matches the skill name/description. However the registry metadata at the top of the evaluation claims no required binaries or env vars, while SKILL.md and scripts clearly require curl, file, jq and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY or a credentials file. That mismatch is an incoherence in packaging (likely sloppy metadata) and should be clarified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to publishing files: build a manifest, POST/PUT to here.now API, upload to presigned URLs, finalize, and write local state (~/.herenow/credentials and .herenow/state.json). The script does not attempt to read arbitrary user files or other credentials. It does instruct agents to call the sign-up endpoint (sending the user's email) which is expected for retrieving a magic link, and it warns about not passing API keys on the command line.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with an included publish.sh. There is no formal install spec. The script instructs users to run a remote installer if jq is missing (curl -fsSL https://here.now/install.sh | bash). Recommending piping a remote script to bash is a high-risk practice — even if hosted on the same domain, it runs code fetched from the network. Also registry metadata omission (see purpose_capability) increases uncertainty about what will be installed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script requires only service-relevant items: curl, file, jq, and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY or ~/.herenow/credentials. Those are proportionate to a publishing tool. The inconsistency between declared required env vars/binaries in the registry metadata (none) and the SKILL.md/script (curl, file, jq, HERENOW_API_KEY) is a packaging concern that should be resolved before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request global or always-on privileges. It writes local state to the working directory (.herenow/state.json) and may store an API key in ~/.herenow/credentials — both are expected for this functionality. The skill does not modify other skills' configs or request system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal) but this skill does not appear to request excessive persistent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: What to consider before installing: 1) Metadata mismatch — the registry claims no required binaries/env but SKILL.md and the script require curl, file, and jq, and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY or ~/.herenow/credentials. Ask the publisher to fix the metadata or confirm requirements. 2) Inspect the included scripts yourself — the repository includes scripts/publish.sh; review it (you already can) and ensure it only does what you expect. 3) Avoid running suggested curl | bash install commands without inspecting the remote install.sh first; if you must, fetch the file and inspect it instead of piping. 4) Be cautious about where you store your API key: prefer creating ~/.herenow/credentials with restrictive permissions rather than passing keys on the command line. 5) Do not enable --allow-nonherenow-base-url or point the tool at unknown base URLs while using an API key (the script has a guard, but overriding it can expose your key). 6) If you have sensitive files in a directory, review them before publishing (this tool will upload whatever you point it at). If you want lower risk, run the script in an isolated environment or container and confirm behavior before saving credentials on your real account.
